title: Food
hook: eating with thanks, sharing with the hungry
tomorrow: God finally answers Job. why does he talk about rain on empty land?

segments.voice: A week of the world: gentleness and respect, work and rest, money is a servant, redeem the time, guard your attention, care for the temple. And a temple gets fed.
screen: `SIX LINES, ONE WEEK.` → `CARE FOR THE TEMPLE.`

segments.voice: Lunch trays, takeout bags, a granola bar eaten at a red light: plenty of meals go by without anyone noticing them. John tells of one that got noticed. A crowd far from town, hungry. A boy has “five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?” And before anything multiplies, Jesus does one small thing. He gives thanks, for a lunch that is clearly not enough.
screen: `MEALS NOBODY NOTICES.` → `FIVE LOAVES, TWO FISHES.` → `THANKS, BEFORE IT'S ENOUGH.`

segments.voice: That's the order John keeps: “And Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed”. Thanks first, while the bread still looks small. Then sharing, until everyone eats. Today's line holds both halves. The thanks says food is a gift before it's a meal. The First Letter to Timothy says it plainly: “every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving.” Christians say grace in different forms: sung, spoken, silent, with the sign of the cross. The sharing says the gift was never for one table only. Isaiah describes the kind of fast God wants: “Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry?” And the first believers in Acts ate together “with gladness and singleness of heart.” Notice how this week's lines show up at a table. Gentleness and respect, eating with a friend who doesn't pray. Money as a servant, buying groceries for someone else. Attention guarded, phone face down, so the meal gets noticed. One table can hold the whole week.
screen: `THANKS FIRST, WHILE IT LOOKS SMALL.` · `RECEIVED WITH THANKSGIVING.` · `DEAL THY BREAD TO THE HUNGRY.` · `ONE TABLE HOLDS THE WEEK.` · then, large: `THANKS AND SHARING.`

segments.voice: Take a bite or a sip of something near you, slowly, and taste it all the way through: the first note, the texture, what stays afterward. Say a quiet thank you, in whatever words are yours. Then bring to mind one person you could share a meal or a snack with this week.
Food. A gift before it's a meal: received with thanks, and passed along to the hungry.
Your line: thanks and sharing, the two things Jesus did with five loaves. That's the week.

howItsDone: Christians say grace before meals in different ways, from a sung blessing to a silent sign of the cross; churches run food pantries and shared meals, and some keep fasts that send what's saved to the hungry.

fork.setup: you made too much soup. your neighbor just lost her job and won't ask anyone for help. what fits thanks and sharing?
options: bring her a container, simply, the way you'd share with a friend.
freeze it; sharing is what the official food drive is for.

fork.reveal: Isaiah: deal thy bread to the hungry. thanks for the gift, then it goes out the door.

original.note: Greek: having given thanks. John 6:11; the same verb family as the church word Eucharist.

trapdoor: what you thought: grace before meals is a polite habit.
what it means: thanks first, while the food looks small, then sharing until everyone eats.
what a scholar hears: John 6:11 uses eucharisteo, gave thanks, the verb behind the word Eucharist; some readers hear the Last Supper in this meal.

chat.meaning: Jesus gave thanks before the bread was shared, and gentleness and respect still hold at a friend's table. Thanks can be quiet and warm.
